headline: Cleveland Commuters Face 12-Second Doug Delays After Ledger Panic
deck: Rumors of a glowing ledger PIN trigger mass exodus, leaving 17 county vehicles stranded. Doug denies responsibility.
article:
Cleveland commuters abandoned federal buildings after whispers that Doug's ledger now required a secret PIN. The usual sign-in ritual collapsed into a scramble, stranding seventeen county vehicles whose drivers chose flight over the standard visual check.

Gladys Hargrove escaped the lobby and later described the sudden shift from routine to alarm. Doug, unmoved at his post, repeated that his role stopped at a nod and carried no codes.

The DMV warned that any invented four-digit entry would force a full ledger reprint and extra hours for the guard. By mid-morning the building stood empty, twelve streets were blocked, and the parked vans earned the nickname "vehicles of despair."

Leanne Trumbull of the Bureau of Civil Absurdities called the episode a minor hitch in an otherwise reliable system and noted that Doug remained on duty. Commuters now refer to the episode as the Ledger-Lock.
author: Patricia Pennington, Senior Satirical Correspondent

oped.title: Hats Off to Doug: The Real Culprits in Cleveland's 12-Second Crisis
oped.author: Sir Reginald Trustworthy III, PhD in Unbreakable Honor from Doug University
oped.body:
The delays stem from commuters who treat a simple nod as an existential threat. Doug's twelve-second pause rewards steady nerves; the exodus only proved how quickly the honor system unravels when people invent PINs that were never requested.

The rumor appears to have been spread by commuters whose wide-brimmed hats prevent a clear view of their faces. Transparent headgear would let Doug confirm identities at a glance and keep the line moving. The stranded vehicles belong to the same group that fled, not to any failure on the guard's part. My own parking spot was delayed, which is the only real inconvenience here.

classifieds.text: Temporary stand-in needed at the transit lot while seventeen vehicles await retrieval. Applicant must maintain a straight face during the standard twelve-second visual check.
2019 county bus left mid-route after the morning ledger rumor. First buyer who accepts the honor-system terms takes possession; Doug has seen the keys.
Briefcase of handwritten ledgers recovered from the lobby scramble. Describe any entry you recall; no PIN required for return.
Apology issued by the rider whose remark about a glowing ledger emptied the building and left the vans behind. The honor system remains in force.

Stranded driver: 'Your say-so just stranded seventeen cars for twelve seconds. Again.'

stories.headline: Stranded County Vans Reported Missing After 17 Vehicles Left at Doug's Ledger Table
stories.deck: Deputies cite honor-system policy as reason no charges filed against departing commuters.
stories.article:
Seventeen county vans sit untouched outside the transit building following the morning rush prompted by the ledger rumor. Fuel cards and logs remained inside under the usual clipboard protocol.

Deputies recorded the departures as voluntary and logged the vans under "temporarily relocated by mutual understanding." Doug noted each exit without further action.

real_world_echo: Mirrors 'More than 300,000 flee wildfires in France and Spain' as commuters flee offices en masse over glowing-ledger PIN rumors, triggering regional access shutdowns
